overview.description: Boomke Wies is a Belgian Whist game for four players in fixed partnerships with an auction to determine the trump suit. Players bid a number of tricks (7 to 13) they commit to winning. The highest bidder leads to the first trick and the suit of that lead becomes trump. The special bid 'Boom' (committing to win all 13 tricks) scores 5 points but costs 5 on failure. The game also features 'Meetje' â€” a fallback when no one bids, where the dealer simply chooses trumps and majority of tricks wins 1 point.

history.origins: Boomke Wies is a Belgian card game from the Whist family, played in fixed partnerships with an auction mechanic. It is distinct from classic Whist through its bidding system, though a simpler non-bidding variant exists that closely mirrors traditional Whist.
timeline: Traditional: Evolved from the Whist family in Belgium.
Present: Actively played in Belgian clubs and tournaments. The International World Whist Association organises tournaments.
history.evolution: The game exists in two forms: the auction version (described here) and a simpler version without bidding that essentially IS classic Whist with turned-up trump. The auction version adds significant strategic depth.
history.cultural: Part of the rich Belgian card game tradition alongside Wiezen, Kleurenwiezen, and other Whist variants. Tournament play is organised by the International World Whist Association (IWWA).

setup.players: 4 players in fixed partnerships. Teams determined at start: each player takes a portion of the shuffled deck and shows the bottom card â€” two lowest pair up, two highest pair up.
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Cards rank A-K-Q-J-10-9-8-7-6-5-4-3-2 (high to low).
setup.dealing: 13 cards each, dealt in batches: either 4-4-5 or 5-4-4 per player. Dealer may choose to shuffle or not. Player to dealer's right cuts.

rules.objective: Win tricks according to your team's bid, or prevent the opposing team from making theirs.
rules.gameplay: Players bid in order from dealer's left; lowest bid 7, highest Boom (13). Pass or bid higher; once you pass you may not bid again. When three have passed, dealer must bid 7, bid Boom, or declare Meetje. Highest bidder leads to the first trick; the suit of that card is trump. Each trick: follow suit if possible; no obligation to beat or trump when void. Trick won by highest trump in it, or highest of led suit if no trump. Winner of each trick leads to the next. After 13 tricks, score by bid and tricks won; then next hand or end of round.
keyRules: Bid a number of tricks (7-13); highest bidder picks trump by leading.
No suit mentioned in bidding â€” partners can't know each other's preferred trump.
Boom (13) is the only bid above 9 worth making when three players passed (same score for 7-9).
Meetje: no-bid fallback where dealer leads and majority wins.
Follow suit required; no obligation to head or trump when void.

strategy.basic: Bid conservatively â€” bidding 7 gives the same score as 8 or 9. Only bid higher than 7 if you're sure of 10+ tricks. Boom is high risk/reward.
strategy.intermediate: Since no suit is mentioned during bidding, coordinate trump choice carefully. If your partner bid before you, their lead will reveal their preferred suit. Don't overbid when partner has already committed.
strategy.advanced: Defensive play against Boom bids is critical: winning a single trick gives your team 5 points. When opponents bid Boom, play your strongest card to the first trick. In Meetje, the dealer has an advantage knowing they'll choose trumps â€” bid 7 instead if you have a clear trump suit.
tips: Bidding 8 or 9 gives no advantage over 7 â€” only bid higher if you expect 10+ tricks.
Boom gives 5 points but creates enormous swings â€” use sparingly.
Against Boom, winning ONE trick is worth 10 points of swing (5 to you, -5 to them).
In Meetje, majority wins 1 point with no downside â€” the safest possible outcome.

list.name: Boomke Wies Without Bidding
list.description: Simpler version: deal 4-4-4-1 batches, dealer's last card turned face-up as trump. Player left of dealer leads. Each team scores 1 point per trick won. Essentially classic Whist.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Variation is described in rules text only; it uses the same core engine with no structured overrides configured yet.

difficulty.easy: Bids conservatively (never above 7). Follows suit. Plays highest card when winning seems possible.
difficulty.medium: Evaluates hand strength for bid level. Understands Boom risk/reward. Basic defensive play. Coordinates lead with trump preference.
difficulty.hard: Optimal bidding based on hand evaluation. Advanced defensive play against Boom (maximise chance of winning one trick). Partnership signaling through play. Card counting. Exploits Meetje when favourable.

considerations: Bidding without announcing suit creates unique partnership communication challenge.
Asymmetric scoring (7-9 pay the same) simplifies bid decisions but adds defensive complexity.
Boom creates massive point swings â€” AI must evaluate risk correctly.
Meetje is strategically significant: knowing when NOT to bid is as important as knowing when to bid.

customActions.description: Dealer deals 13 cards each clockwise in batches of 4-4-5 or 5-4-4; player to dealer's right cuts.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only. Dealer may shuffle or not; then deal in chosen batch order.

customActions.description: Bid a number of tricks (7 to 12) committing your team to win at least that many if you choose trump; bid must be higher than current highest bid.
customActions.constraints: Bidding phase. Auction continues until three players have passed; final bidder leads first trick and its suit is trump.

customActions.description: Bid Boom (13 tricks): commit to win all 13 tricks; scores 5 on success, -5 on failure (opponents score 5).
customActions.constraints: Available to dealer when first three passed. Only bid above 9 when three passed that gives higher score than 7.

customActions.description: As dealer when first three passed: declare Meetje; you lead first trick (suit is trump). Team with majority of tricks scores 1; no penalty for taking fewer.
customActions.constraints: Dealer only when first three players all passed. No extra benefit for more than 7 tricks.

customActions.description: System evaluates whether bidding team made their bid and applies point rules (1/2/3 for 7-9/10-12/13 tricks; -1/-2 or -5 for failure; Meetje: majority wins 1).
customActions.constraints: System phase after all 13 tricks played.

customActions.description: System awards points to teams based on bid result and tricks won; tournament round ends after time limit, tie broken by extra deal.
customActions.constraints: System phase; applies scoring table then starts next deal or ends round.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for Boomke Wies (Dutch trick-taking game) with trump and point scoring.
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). Trump is determined by the deal or bid; follow suit when able. Standard trick order applies; point cards (e.g. tens, aces) are counted for the score.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit in standard order (ace high down to two). Trick and point values follow the game rules; the goal is to take tricks and reach a target score in Boomke Wies.
engine.dealPattern: 4-4-5 or 5-4-4 per player; dealer may choose order.
